question: Will the Oleshky truce hold, yes or no?
hook_lines: Aid in, civilians out from 29 Oct

lines.text: Melania Trump has secured a local ceasefire in Oleshky, the White House says.
It starts on the twenty ninth of October, to let aid in and civilians out.
Oleshky is Russian-occupied, across the Dnipro River from Kherson.
About twenty four thousand people lived there before the war.
The White House says only seventeen hundred to two thousand remain, mostly elderly.
AP reports there is no electricity, heat or running water, and food and medicine have been scarce for months.
In twenty twenty three, floodwater from the Kakhovka dam swamped the town.
Melania Trump calls it a front-line war city on the brink of disaster.

scene.quote: Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster.

lines.text: Ukraine's ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets has confirmed the deal.
He says the operation will be gradual, and extremely difficult to implement.

scene.quote: It is extremely difficult to implement.

lines.text: The Kremlin says the Russian military is coordinating the timing.
Melania Trump says some residents may choose Russia and some Ukraine, and an American media group will go with the teams.
Separately, the Kremlin says three-way talks with Ukraine and the US are planned in Abu Dhabi in early November.
Will the Oleshky truce hold, yes or no?
